messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: kinds of variables + more warnings
parts:
After the really useful discussion Wednesday, I'd like to add one
more kind of variable, a derived quantity computed once per sample.
I'll also rename "derived" to "transformed", leaving us with
the following six blocks per Stan program, all of which are
optional other than model and parameters.

// read once per chain (double)
data { declarations }

// computed once per chain (double)
transformed data { declarations statements }

// read once per leapfrog step with transforms (auto-dif var)
parameters { declarations }

// computed per leapfrog step (auto-dif var)
transformed parameters { declarations statements }

// computed once per leapfrog step (auto-dif var)
model { statements }

// computed once per saved sample (double)
derived quantities { declarations statements }

I indicated how often each of the block of statements
are run and the type of variables they run over (auto-dif
is much more expensive). Computing the log probabilty
(including log Jacobian determinants of transforms) and
its gradient will dominate -- it's most expense and computed
per leapfrog step.

I'll add some stricter error testing, like transformed
parameters on the left-hand-side of a sample or
actual parameters on the left-hand-side of an assignment
and flag them as warnings by default.

- Bob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] kinds of variables + more warnings
parts:
B
Interesting. In many ways, the explicit rules ("read once per chain", etc) are clearer than the names ("data", etc).
Also, I was thinking more about the error/warning checking, and my current thought is that, with this clarity in declarations, I'm not so concerned about rules such as "transformed parameters can't be on the left side of a distributional assignment". If that kind of warning-checking takes effort on your part then maybe it's not worth doing right now. After all, we'll probably have a better sense of what the dangerous errors are, once Stan-R is working and we (and others) are using it.
See you
A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] kinds of variables + more warnings
parts:
The warnings aren't too hard to push through.
The big one is reassigning to a parameter because
it'll act like a local variable, not a node in the
graphical model, and I think that'll confuse people
if we don't warn them. Naive users will also forget
to apply Jacobians when sampling a transformed
parameter.

I'm almost done with the once-per-chain derived
quantities. We'll allow the user to specify which
parameters, transformed parameters, and derived
quantities get dumped, defaulting to just dumping
them all.

I also plan to add some variable-type abbreviations,

boolean = int(0,1)
categorical(K) = int(1,K)
ordinal(K) = int(1,K)
probability = double(0,1)
correlation = double(-1,1)

Mainly I think they'll make the models easier to read.

I went with Gelman-and-Hill-style ordered positive
values for logit cutpoints.

ordered(K) = vector(K) with Jacobian

JAGS uses an implicit distribution by generating K independent
values then sorting them, which is very different than what
Stan's doing -- letting each have a log differnce, starting from
zero.

- Bob
